summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on redesigning the existing ClickHouse cluster, moving away from a sharded architecture to one based on replicas. The proposed new setup involves three distinct machines: `processing` (for data ingestion and recalculation), `playground` (for running various data models/queries), and `front-end` (smaller machine with fast CPU). 

The current sharding mechanism is deemed unnecessary overhead. By using replicas instead of shards, the system gains resilience; if one machine fails, data can be redirected to another replica without service interruption.

Regarding implementation, it was noted that all machines could potentially accept data ingestion, allowing for maximum redundancy. The `processing` machine currently handles streaming recalculation (real-time processing of raw data into session types: box, facility, facility_master) and is planned to handle additional tasks like hourly aggregation, real-time modeling using ClickHouse external user functions, and anomaly/permanent detection jobs.
decisions: Transition the cluster from a sharded architecture to one based on replicas.
Implement three dedicated machines: processing, playground, and front-end.
action_items: Discuss implementation details of the cluster redesign with minimal or zero downtime.
